name: TM1637
full_name: Titan Micro TM1637 LED Drive Control IC (4-digit module)
description: The TM1637 is a low-cost LED driver with a built-in display memory and keypad-scan capability, sold mainly as a 4-digit 7-segment clock-style module with a 4-pin header (VCC, GND, DIO, CLK). It talks over a custom two-wire protocol that looks like I2C electrically but has no device address and uses a different ack scheme, so a hardware I2C peripheral cannot drive it directly. The driver handles multiplexing and 8-level brightness internally, so the MCU just sends segment data and a brightness command. Its bit-banged two-wire interface and the iconic clock module with a center colon make it the go-to for hobby clocks and counters.

pins.name: CLK
pins.description: two-wire clock line (bit-banged, not hardware I2C)

extra.max_grids: 6 grids x 8 segments on bare chip
extra.keyscan: up to 16 keys (chip feature, usually unused on display modules)

typical_application: A 4-digit clock or counter readout driven from any two spare GPIO pins (CLK, DIO) using a TM1637 library; the colon segment makes it ideal for HH:MM clocks.
gotchas: NOT real I2C - it has no slave address and a nonstandard ack, so you must bit-bang it or use a TM1637-specific library, not the Wire library
pin header order varies between board vendors; always read the silkscreen rather than assuming CLK/DIO positions
the digit/segment address mapping is fixed by the module wiring; the colon is usually bit 7 of digit 2
DIO is open-drain style and bidirectional; driving it as a hard push-pull output can cause contention during the ack bit
brightness must be set with a command; a fresh module may power up dim or blank until configured
